Calibrate a declared allocation model from explicit starting points

Source: R/06-ae_workflow.R
fit_allocation.Rd

Count targets and loss choice are separate. Weighted SSE retains the existing default; Poisson is explicit. Custom loss/gradient functions pass through. Observation-indexed loss arguments must be in canonical order. Starts, boundaries, failed runs and disagreement retain the existing multistart result; a selected fit is not a claim of identification or global optimality.

Usage

fit_allocation(
  model,
  observed,
  starts,
  lower,
  upper,
  output = "utilization",
  loss = "weighted_sse",
  loss_args = list(),
  loss_grad = NULL,
  gradient = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

model

A corrected CLM declared over checked prepared inputs. A kernel declared smooth = FALSE cannot be fitted.

observed

Numeric vector or origin-by-facility matrix. Named axes match declared IDs independently; unnamed axes are positional. Keep all IDs and use NA for unobserved entries. The count-valued utilization, flow and utilization_by_group targets reject negative nonmissing observations; fractional counts are allowed. Other output domains pass through to the existing fitter. For utilization_by_group (a model with demand groups) a facility-by-group matrix of observed counts with both axes named (group columns by group ID, facility rows by facility ID, any order).

starts

A finite positive matrix, one explicit independent start per row, with exactly the named model parameter columns. No random starts are added. Each start must lie inside the supplied positive bounds.

lower, upper

Complete named positive parameter bounds with lower < upper. For a declared kernel, the starts and bounds of sigma must lie within the bounds of the declaration.

output

Exact model output to calibrate; default facility utilization. flow is expected origin-facility counts, while allocation is an inside probability operator. Requesting counts does not select a likelihood. utilization_by_group is the expected count of each group at each facility (a model with demand groups, see clm_allocation()). The group-specific parameters of such a model (sigma.<group>, v0.<group>, from by_group) can be fitted only to this output, with observed counts for every group that has one and positive demand in that group; aggregated targets leave them multimodal and weakly identified, so the fit is refused (before any start) with a message naming the parameters. Fix them with clm_allocation(fixed = ), or fit shared parameters to any target.

loss

"weighted_sse", "poisson", or a function accepting predicted and observed values. Weighted SSE divides squared residuals by observed+eta, with eta=1 by default. Poisson omits the data-only log-factorial constant. It floors modelled counts at eps (loss_args), 1e-250 by default, only to avoid the log of zero; cells with positive observed counts modelled below the floor are reported with a warning, because the loss is capped there. Fits made before this default used 1e-9; pass loss_args = list(eps = 1e-9) to reproduce them. Joint fitting does not force total matching.

loss_args

Named auxiliary arguments passed to loss callbacks. For loss = "poisson" an eps of 1e-250 is added when none is given; other arguments pass unchanged. Any observation-indexed values must already follow canonical observed order.

loss_grad

Optional matching parameter-gradient callback. Built-in choices supply their existing analytic loss-gradient adapters. A custom loss requires its own loss_grad when gradient=TRUE; none is invented.

gradient

Logical; use the existing implicit sensitivity route when TRUE. FALSE retains the underlying fitter's default behavior.

...

Named multistart or fitting controls, including solver tolerances, optimizer control, keep_fits and descriptive disagreement tolerances.

Value

The existing ae_multistart_fit, retaining selected fit, all per-start diagnostics, boundaries, warnings/errors and descriptive disagreement.

Details

A model whose decay kernel was declared with smooth = FALSE (see decay_kernel()) is refused, because fitting needs a kernel that is smooth in sigma. Evaluate such a kernel at fixed parameters with evaluate_allocation(), for example over a grid of sigma and v0.

See also

allocation-fit-methods for methods on saved fits.
